vintage_conflict_note: VINTAGE CONFLICT (preserved & flagged): Whisky Auctioneer bottle hub and Whiskyhunter state distilled 1990; Whisky Auctioneer product listing 1280618 is titled 'Rosebank 1991 31 Year Old Release #2' and Whiskybase carries alt slug 'rosebank-1991'. Both 1990 and 1991 are reported in sources; unresolved. Age (31yo) and bottling year (2022) are consistent across sources.

tasting.nose: Champagne gold. Banana cake, cherry blossom and lavender with malt and virgin oak shavings; baked apple, peach and apple butter over a grassy/herbaceous backbone; nutty, mossy, furniture polish giving way to floral elderflower and lemon with a light briny edge.
tasting.palate: Velvety soft dried grass reminiscent of chamomile tea; wild strawberries and sweet lemon citrus over toasted marshmallow; toffee, glazed nuts, vanilla cream, baked apple, citrus and a little cocoa; tea leaf, sandalwood, vanilla cookies and baking spice, with modest oak tannin.
tasting.finish: Bubbly champagne and oak with a slight medicinal flavour; well-balanced, with a roasty edge balancing the sweetness.
tasting.narrative: Release Two is, in Words of Whisky's phrase, 'an ideal of what traditional Lowland whisky is' — delicate yet expressive, more vocal on the palate than the nose. Critics scored it strongly (Whisky Auctioneer 91, Whiskybase 90.42) and it has gathered competition metal. A poised, floral 31-year-old that rewards patience over power. Verdict: an excellent Lowland keeper, slightly softer-spoken than Release One.
